newsitem.title: BELGIUM: COBEPA KEEN TO KEEP GOOD RELATIONS WITH FLANDERS.
newsitem.headline: COBEPA KEEN TO KEEP GOOD RELATIONS WITH FLANDERS.

text.p: Belgian holding company Cobepa said on Monday that it would keep good relations with Flemish financial groups, despite its planned split with Flemish holding company Gevaert .

"The Almanij-Gevaert group and we will remain on friendly terms...we are not losing our contact with the leading Flemish families," Cobepa chief executive officer Pierre Scohier told a news conference, where Paribas chairman Andre Levy-Lang was also present.
Cobepa is 60-percent owned by French Paribas .
On Friday, Cobepa cut its years-old ties with Gevaert, which will come under the wings of fellow Flemish holding company Almanij .
In a complex deal involving a series of share swaps in the autumn, Cobepa will keep half of Gevaert's assets, while Gevaert itself will become majority-owned by Almanij.
Currently, Gevaert is 35-percent owned by Cobepa and affiliates and 25 percent by families who act in concert with Cobepa. The rest is owned by the public.

Scohier said that Cobepa would keep nurturing close relations with the leading Flemish families in the financial world, as several of these families would remain partners in Cobepa or in Cobepa units.
Scohier said that he saw no competition between Gevaert and Cobepa-unit Ibel in the merchant banking business.
"Traditionaly, Gevaert has never been interested in mall and medium sized companies," Scohier said. Ibel will focus on investments in small and medium-sized Flemish companies.
He added that if Ibel wanted to take on larger acquisitions, it would have to do this together with other partners. "And Cobepa is always there as a back-up for bigger deals," he said.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
